title: Microsoft Copilot: Copilot Code builds software and apps from plain-language descriptions
summary: The spending-policy prerequisite is documented, but it does not establish that Copilot Code needs a fresh administrator opt-in. Existing spending policies automatically include newly supported services by default, so waiting can extend access and spending without a new Code-specific policy. The roadmap facts and the cited control paths, endpoint and macOS policy keys are supported.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Copilot Code is admin-opt-in because its exposure is created by a policy the administrator writes, not by waiting.
claims.quote: When a spending policy has Auto-apply new services turned on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy as they become available.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Replace the last three sentences of Why it matters with: 'A spending policy is required, but that does not necessarily mean a new Copilot Code opt-in: existing spending policies have Auto-apply new services selected by default and can automatically include Code. Review existing policy coverage before assuming users cannot build. Microsoft has not stated whether the Code tab itself is on or off in a new tenant.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits and https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits.

claims.claim: The qualified general spending-policy create API is POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies with the listed body properties.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies
In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a spendingPolicy object with a concrete @odata.type. Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.
